subject: OrbitPay latency regression — closure, timeline, and mitigation ledger

From: Olga Petrova <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orbitpay.com>, Samira El-Khateeb <samira@orbitpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitPay latency regression — closure, timeline, and mitigation ledger

Hi Alex / Samira,

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated the latency regression you reported on May 16. Below is a concise, customer-facing summary of what we found, the timeline, and the actions we've taken or committed to. I attached a one-page timeline (orbitpay_rca_timeline.pdf) for your records.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Impact: 03:05–05:40 UTC on 2027-05-16 — elevated 95th/99th percentile latency and increased request timeouts for the /v1/generate endpoint used by OrbitPay payment validation. Estimated ~18 minutes of partial payment delays per affected shard.
- Root cause: A canary configuration pushed to the batching router disabled cross-request KV sharing in ~40% of routing decisions, significantly reducing effective batching and overwhelming a small subset of inference workers.
- Customer impact: increased token latency and ~1.6% of requests hit retry thresholds, causing downstream payment processing delays.

Timeline (high level)
- 2027-05-16 02:48 UTC — OrbitPay alerts via PagerDuty; initial spike observed in front-end error rate.
- 2027-05-16 03:05 UTC — degraded latency confirmed; auto-scaling partially engaged but insufficient due to skewed worker utilization.
- 2027-05-16 04:20 UTC — Canary configuration identified as diverging from production profile; mitigations applied (partial rollback).
- 2027-05-16 05:40 UTC — Full rollback completed; error rates and latency returned to baseline.
- 2027-05-17 07:00 UTC — Internal RCA draft completed; shared with engineering and reliability leads.

Root cause details (concise)
- A canary roll introduced a gating flag in the batching router that inadvertently prevented the router from grouping short-sequence requests across user sessions. This reduced average batch size by ~60% for a subset of traffic routed to three worker pools.
- Reduced batching amplified per-token GPU overhead and caused queueing on those pools. With skewed routing, autoscaling decisions used total queue length which undercounted localized pressure, so additional workers were not provisioned quickly enough.

Actions taken (completed)
1) Immediate rollback of the canary that removed KV-sharing gating (completed 2027-05-16 05:40 UTC).
2) Emergency route-level throttle to shed non-critical background traffic during recovery window (completed).
3) Manual rebalancing of routing table to spread traffic more evenly across pools (completed).

Actions committed (short and medium term)
- Short (2–5 days): Implement server-side canary validation that runs simulation checks against historical sequence distributions before gating flags are accepted; add a per-pool queue depth metric to the autoscaler.
- Medium (2–3 weeks): Release a batching router safety net that rejects configurations which can reduce average batch size below a safe threshold; add canary cancellation hooks to rollback mid-rollouts automatically if localized pressure spikes.
- Customer-facing (this week): Share the attached timeline PDF and the configuration diff we will apply (mitigation-config-diff.patch) to demonstrate the fix steps.

Credits / remediation
- We understand the operational impact to OrbitPay. Once you confirm the impact window and the customer-visible effects, we will propose a service credit in line with our SLA terms. I'll follow up with proposed credit calculations by Wednesday.

If you'd like a quick 30-minute walkthrough of the timeline and the technical mitigation with our SREs and the product team, I'm available tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT.

Best,
Olga Petrova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Alex — quick technical addendum and attachments.

Thanks for the questions; see items below and attached patch (mitigation-config-diff.patch). Also uploaded the corresponding traces and flame graphs to the shared folder: https://redwood.internal/drive/orbitpay/incident-2027-05-17.

- Tail traces: we retained full traces for the window you provided. The majority of high-latency samples correlate with worker pools A3/A4 where the reduced batch sizes were observed. We include example trace ids in the Drive folder.
- Canary validation scope: the short-term validation we are deploying checks sequence-length distribution and estimated batch size for any router gating flag. This is not a global type system change, but it will prevent configuration changes that materially reduce effective batching. The medium-term safety net will be broader.
- Service credit: Olga — per SLA, outages that meet the defined threshold qualify for a prorated credit. Technical team recommends calculating on impacted tokens and request volume for the 03:05–05:40 UTC window; I can produce a CSV export if OrbitPay wants a precise breakdown.

Attachments:
- mitigation-config-diff.patch (config diff and notes)

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra

Alex / Samira — following up with the final customer-facing artifacts and next steps.

1) Attached you will find the one-page timeline (orbitpay_rca_timeline.pdf) and the config diff (mitigation-config-diff.patch). The Drive link contains the full traces and the CSV export of affected request counts per region.
2) Service credit proposal: based on the affected token volume during the 03:05–05:40 UTC window, we propose a 15% credit on the affected API calls for the billing period in which the incident occurred. If you prefer, we can instead apply a one-time credit equal to the prorated cost of the affected requests. Please confirm which option you prefer and we'll generate the formal credit note.
3) Operational rollback: the short-term canary validation was deployed to production at 2027-05-19 11:10 UTC and is currently active. We'll monitor with elevated alerts for 72 hours and report daily to this thread.
4) Follow-up: I've scheduled a 30-minute incident review for Thursday 2027-05-20 10:00 PT with our SRE and product leads (invite sent). Please tell me if that slot doesn't work.

We understand this had a real impact on your payment flow. We're committed to preventing recurrence and to making the remediation transparent.

Thanks,
Olga
